title: Who influenced whom among early tenors: Hawk, Happy and Prince Robinson
summary: Everyone heard Hawk first; Prince Robinson started at the Calvert Palace and was influenced by Hawk.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: Well, who do you think -- I mean now there's a good question. I mean who do you think Chu had to influence him? I mean by that time, I suppose, he must have heard Hawk.
Oh, well, all means, sure he heard Hawk. He heard Hawk before he heard Ben. we all heard Hawk was up before Ben.
Yeah, but earlier on you were talking about Hawk and Prince Robinson. Well, there was a time when that was Hawk and Prince Robinson were two of the best (unintelligible).

You had to get -- got to get by all three of us. That was the whole question, tough thing. They made it that way. Whenever Hawk and I would be playing, we wouldn't pay that no mind, but that was the proving grounds.
Well, now wait a minute. Prince was with McKinney's, right?
Well, he left. He went with McKinney's in later years.
Well, where was he making his name

He started, him and Bob Robertson, the one that sponsored me in masons, they were working with fellow named Bendy Howard, had a band on 140th Street and Lenox, called the Calvert Palace. It was a good band. It was eight pieces.

Bendy Howard. And that's when I -- they thought that Prince Robertson and Bob Robertson were brothers, but they weren't, because the both of them came out of Virginia. But they were no relation. And they had a fine band, a group, good band. And that was back, oh, that was around --
Well, I mean did Prince -- do you think -- I mean you yourself had heard Hawk.
So you were influenced by him, naturally, since you had got a -- you were coming off clarinet onto tenor.
Well now, when -- what -- I mean do you think Prince was influenced by Hawk?
I think he was because he -- he was playing clarinet like I was. When he came to New York, he was playing then clarinet and tenor.
So really, I mean Hawk was like first with that tone.
Right. He was first of most of us fellows. He influenced most of us fellows, because --
